text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 1.8% today, giving back some of yesterday's sharp 4.6% gain after hitting $463 on October 8th. The pullback likely reflects uncertainty around the geopolitical moves announced over the past two days: Trump's "energy ceasefire" between Russia and Ukraine and the reported deal to import Russian diesel to ease U.S. fuel prices. For a refiner, a sudden flood of cheaper imported diesel is a potential headwind—it could weaken margins on fuel the company produces domestically, which explains why the stock jumped on October 8th (when energy markets were tighter) but reversed today as the supply implications became clearer.

The broader context matters here: U.S. refineries are running at 92.7% capacity and diesel inventories are relatively lean at 105 million barrels, so the market had priced in tight supply and strong refiner margins. The Trump-Putin diesel deal undermines that tight-supply story. The stock is still up 15.6% over two weeks, so today's retreat may simply be profit-taking on an outsized rally, but the geopolitical supply shift is the concrete driver of the reversal.
